Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`), estVoice (s: the predicted voice length, tools/estimate.py; replaced by the real voice once tools/voice.py has run).

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Adivamshavatarana sub-parva. CHECKED AGAINST CE 1.58.1–51 and 1.59.1–4 (GRETIL e-text of the constituted text, lab/ce; star passages and appendix lines are apparatus and were not used; Ganguli (vulgate) only as a reading aid): Janamejaya asks why the godlike warriors were born on earth (1.58.1–2); Vaishampayana: this is a secret of the gods, I will tell it (1.58.3: `secret`); Jamadagni's son (Parashurama) had made the earth empty of kshatriyas twenty-one times (1.58.4: `kings`, his name on a plaque); kshatriya women had sons by brahmins and the kshatriya line grew again (1.58.5–8: "a new line"); it ruled by dharma (1.58.12–13), Indra rained in season (1.58.14), no one died as a child (1.58.15: "no child died young"), in a krita age (1.58.24); the earth filled with creatures to the seas (1.58.16, 24); then asuras were born among the kings: the sons of Diti, beaten many times in battle by the gods and cast down from their sovereignty (1.58.25–26: `asuras`), born among men and in cattle, horses, asses, camels, buffalo, beasts of prey, elephants and deer (1.58.27–28: "as beasts"); some were born as mighty, arrogant kings (1.58.30–31) who oppressed all four orders and every creature (1.58.32–34: `crushed`); the earth could not bear herself (1.58.29: `weight`, the turn), nor could wind, serpents or mountains hold her (1.58.36); weighed down and afraid she went for refuge to Brahma (1.58.37: `went`), who sat among gods, sages, gandharvas and apsarases (1.58.38–39), and petitioned him before the world-guardians (1.58.40: the CE gives her NO words; she does not speak here); he already knew her purpose (1.58.41–42: `knew`); he told her he would appoint all the heaven-dwellers to it (1.58.44), dismissed her, and commanded the gods: to cast off this earth's burden, be born on her with your portions, each apart, for strife (1.58.46: `command`, condensed; virodhaya, "to fight", is on the plaque); he said the same to gandharvas and apsarases (1.58.47); Indra and the rest accepted (1.58.48) and went to Narayana in Vaikuntha (1.58.49); Indra said to him: descend with a portion; and Hari said: so be it (1.58.51: `agreed`; Indra is on the plaque); the heaven-dwellers came down in turn and were born in the lines of brahmin seers and royal seers (1.59.3–4: the cliffhanger; "demons alike" is 1.58.25–31 and 1.61.4–61). NOT IN THE CE and not used: the Earth in the form of a cow (the word gam at 1.58.11 means the earth); any speech of the Earth. "Golden age" is not said: the text's word is krita.
structure: As from episode 41 (script/ARC-41-50.md, script/ARC-51-60.md): COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words; the hook style rotates and never repeats the episode before; no episode of this batch opens on fire) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band → the episode stands alone (every name has an identifier in "names", shown as a plaque) → one question closed (loop.answeredBy), the previous one answered by 15 s (loop.prevAnsweredBy) → turn at 40–60 % after a real silence, a second silence where the story allows → one face close-up with a change of emotion → one signature shot → the cliffhanger with the source line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band that dissolves into frame 1. Per line: pal (the colour script: no hue for more than two lines), cam (≥ 4 distinct moves), tr (transitions born from the medium), amb / foley / music (three sound layers; ambLead / ambLag = J- and L-cuts). Gate: tools/gate.mjs.

names.Earth: the goddess who bears the world

loop.hookQuestion: Why were gods born as men?
loop.prevQuestion: Why were godlike heroes born on earth?
loop.openQuestion: Which god was born as which hero?

strings.recapLine: Asked why godlike heroes were born on earth, the teller answered.

lines.text: Why were gods born as men?
lines.say: Why were gods [p:80] born as men?
lines.note: COLD OPEN (a question card over the image; no fire): the Earth as a woman, large in the frame, bent under a dark mass that rests on her shoulders: a hill of tiny towers, spears and beasts. A tilt up from her bowed head to the mass. The card low.

lines.speaker: vaishampayana
lines.text: "To lift a burden from the Earth. It is a secret of the gods."
lines.say: To lift a burden from the Earth. [p:260] It is a secret of the gods.
lines.note: FRAME with the unvoiced recap band (top): the hall of the snake sacrifice at night in teal: Vaishampayana (plaque: Vaishampayana · the teller, Vyasa's student) answers the king (plaque: Janamejaya · the king who asked), a finger raised: a secret. Answers episode 50's last line by 5 s.

lines.text: After the old warrior kings were wiped out, a new line ruled by the law. No child died young.
lines.say: After the old warrior kings were wiped out, [p:150] a new line ruled by the law. [p:260] No child died young.
lines.note: STORY 1 · NEW LIGHT (meadow-spring): a crane down over a bright land: fields, a young king on a low seat giving judgment, children running. Small, top left, for one second: an axe-bearing figure walking away over a hill (plaque: Parashurama · the axe-bearing sage; sub: twenty-one times · Adi 1.58.4).

lines.text: Then the asuras, beaten by the gods and cast out of heaven, began to be born on earth.
lines.say: Then the asuras, [p:100] beaten by the gods [p:60] and cast out of heaven, [p:150] began to be born on earth.
lines.note: STORY 2 · NEW LIGHT (venom-violet): a tilt down a dark sky: broad horned figures falling, turning as they fall into points of sickly green light that sink into the land below (tag: asuras · the gods' old enemies).

lines.text: As proud kings, and as beasts, they crushed all that lived.
lines.say: As proud kings, [p:100] and as beasts, [p:150] they crushed all that lived.
lines.note: STORY 3 (dice-vermilion): a lateral track: a huge crowned king on a chariot, green-eyed, rolling over the land; behind him bull, horse and elephant shapes with the same green eye; small hermits and farmers run.

lines.text: The Earth could not bear her own weight.
lines.say: The Earth [p:80] could not bear her own weight.
lines.note: STORY 4 · THE TURN (≈ 45 %) after a real silence · THE CLOSE-UP: the hook's figure again, near: the Earth's face under the mass (plaque: Earth · the goddess who bears the world): endurance, then fear (the brows lift, the eyes go up), the head sinking a hand's breadth. The word of the turn: BURDEN, clear of her face.

lines.text: Afraid, she went to Brahma, the creator.
lines.say: Afraid, [p:120] she went to Brahma, [p:80] the creator.
lines.note: STORY 5 · THE SIGNATURE SHOT · NEW LIGHT (memory-indigo into rose): a crane up and back: she climbs, small, a long stair of cloud toward a great seated four-faced figure on a lotus, large in the upper frame, ringed by rows of small bright gods (plaque: Brahma · the creator).

lines.text: He already knew why she had come.
lines.say: He already knew [p:100] why she had come.
lines.note: STORY 6 (brahma-rose): Brahma large and near, his front face calm, a hand lifting in reassurance before she can speak; she kneels at the foot of the frame, hands joined (the text gives her no words here).

lines.speaker: brahma
lines.text: "Gods: be born on earth, each with a part of yourself, and lift her burden."
lines.say: Gods: [p:200] be born on earth, [p:100] each with a part of yourself, [p:160] and lift her burden.
lines.note: STORY 7 (sun-white; answers the hook): Brahma's arm sweeps out over the ranks of gods; from each a second, smaller light steps out of his chest and leans toward the dark earth far below (tag: "in parts, each apart, to fight" · Adi 1.58.46).

lines.text: And Narayana himself said: so be it.
lines.say: And Narayana himself [p:120] said: [p:150] so be it.
lines.note: STORY 8 (a second real silence before it; pure-flame): the deep blue of Vaikuntha: Narayana large, dark, yellow-robed, discus and mace, Indra small before him with joined hands (plaques: Narayana · Vishnu, the preserver; Indra · king of the gods). He inclines his head. A pull back.

lines.text: So gods and demons alike were born as men: the heroes and villains of this story.
lines.say: So gods and demons alike [p:60] were born as men: [p:200] the heroes [p:60] and villains of this story.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (the catalog's cliffhanger, corrected: demons too): a green earth by day: lights come down like slow rain and where each lands a small standing figure rises: an archer, a mace-bearer, a crowned prince, a woman; two of them green-eyed. The source line (top).
The NEXT › band over the cliffhanger image, with the source line; dissolve into frame 1.
